prompt: Backend implementation instructions (only). Scope: implement the PUT (update) behavior for the entry resource so that description is treated as: omitted = leave existing value unchanged; null = set database column to SQL NULL; empty string ("") = save the empty string. Preserve creation (POST) behavior unchanged. Do not change any other API semantics. Explicit requirements and constraints to implement: 1) Enforce description maximum length 255 characters when a description value is present and non-null. 2) Never implicitly convert an omitted description to null. 3) Never collapse or convert an empty string to null. 4) The frontend’s “clear” action will send description: null; the backend must accept and store that as NULL. Implementation checklist (step-by-step): 1. Request parsing and presence detection:   - Parse the request JSON into a map/dictionary/object.   - Do not rely on model-binding that overwrites existing entity fields with default/None/NULL when a JSON key is omitted. Instead, detect whether the request JSON explicitly contains the key "description": use a presence check (e.g., hasOwnProperty / key in dict / JsonNode.has("description") / map.containsKey("description")).   - Distinguish three cases:     a) Key absent (omitted) — do not change the description column.     b) Key present with value null — set database column to NULL.     c) Key present with a JSON string (including empty string "") — validate and save that exact string. 2. Validation rules (apply only when the description key is present and not null):   - If the value is not a JSON string type, return HTTP 400 with a clear validation error (e.g., "description must be a string or null").   - If the string length > 255 characters, return HTTP 400 with a clear validation error (e.g., "description length must be <= 255").   - If the string length <= 255 (including length == 0), accept it and continue.   - Do NOT perform automatic conversion of empty string to null, trimming-to-null, or other normalizations that would change the empty-string semantics. 3. Database column nullability:   - Verify the entries.description database column permits NULL. If it does not, create a schema migration to alter the column to be nullable. Document and coordinate this migration with DB release process. (Setting NULL requires DB NULL permissibility.) 4. Update execution:   - Build the UPDATE operation to only include columns for which the client provided an explicit key. Do not blindly write the whole object back to the DB.   - Pseudocode pattern:     let updates = {}     if requestBody.containsKey('description'):       if requestBody['description'] === null:         updates['description'] = NULL     else:       // present and non-null string validated above         updates['description'] = requestBody['description']     // ... include other fields using same presence-check rules if they have the same semantics ...     if updates not empty:       execute SQL UPDATE entries SET <only fields in updates> WHERE id = :id;     else:       // nothing to update; handle according to existing PUT semantics (no-op or return existing resource)  - Use parameterized queries/ORM setters so NULL values are sent as SQL NULL, and strings (including empty string) are sent as string parameters. 5. Avoid framework/ORM pitfalls:   - If your framework's automatic object-to-entity copy treats missing fields as null or 0 and then saves that object, switch to one of these safer methods:     a) Patch-style updates that accept a map of fields to update, or     b) Manual presence-checking followed by explicit set/clear calls on the entity, or     c) Use a JSON tree/JsonNode and inspect has(key) before applying to entity.   - Disable or bypass any middleware that converts empty strings to null (some request preprocessors do this); ensure input remains exactly as provided. 6. Transactional and concurrency considerations:   - Execute the selective update inside the same transaction used previously for updates. Preserve existing locking/optimistic concurrency behavior; do not change concurrency semantics. 7. Error handling and status codes:   - For validation failures (non-string or length > 255) return HTTP 400 with error details.   - If the target entry id does not exist, return the same status code your API already uses for not-found (preserve existing 404 semantics).   - For successful updates keep existing success status semantics (do not change whether you return 200/204 or the updated resource). 8. Tests and acceptance criteria (mandatory tests to add):   - Test A (omit description): Given an existing entry with description = 'X', send PUT without a description key; assert DB description remains 'X' and API returns success.   - Test B (null description): Given an existing entry with description = 'X', send PUT with {"description": null}; assert DB description becomes SQL NULL and API returns success.   - Test C (empty string): Given an existing entry with description = 'X', send PUT with {"description": ""}; assert DB description becomes empty string "" and API returns success.   - Test D (max length): Send PUT with description length = 255; assert success and DB stores exact string.   - Test E (too long): Send PUT with description length = 256; assert HTTP 400 and DB unchanged.   - Test F (non-string): Send PUT with description = 123 (non-string non-null); assert HTTP 400 and DB unchanged.   - Test G (create unaffected): Run existing POST/creation tests to ensure creation rules are unchanged. 9. Logging and audit:   - Log update attempts and include whether description key was omitted/present-null/present-string in the audit log. 10. Documentation and API contract:   - Update backend API documentation to explicitly state:     - Omitting description in PUT leaves it unchanged.     - description: null clears the value to NULL.     - description: "" saves as empty string.     - description maximum length 255.     - Creation (POST) rules are unchanged. Acceptance conditions (explicit):   - Backend passes Tests A–G above.   - Database column accepts NULL values after migration if necessary.   - The backend must not, in any code path, convert an omitted description to NULL or convert an empty string to NULL.   - Validation errors returned for invalid types or length > 255. Implementation notes / examples (language-agnostic patterns):   - Presence check: use requestJson.containsKey('description') or equivalent.   - Null check: if requestJson['description'] === null -> set SQL NULL.   - String validation: if typeof value !== 'string' -> validation error; else if value.length > 255 -> validation error; else use value (including empty string). Delivery checklist before merge:   - Unit tests for validation and presence-handling.   - Integration test hitting real DB verifying NULL vs empty string vs unchanged.   - DB migration (if required) to allow NULL on description column.   - API docs update. Do not implement or assume any additional behavior not described above; do not change create (POST) rules; do not invent any alternate payload semantics.
